docs.title: About
docs.text:
Defender is a tower defense game where you place towers to stop waves of enemies from reaching your base. Built from scratch in C++20 with SFML for rendering and audio.

  • 🎮 Classic tower defense gameplay
  • 🏗️ Clean C++20 architecture (concepts, spans, RAII, variants)
  • 🧪 Tested with GoogleTest + CTest
  • 🚀 CI/CD via GitHub Actions

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
BuildTest

cmake --build build --parallel
./build/src/defender

cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug
cmake --build build --parallel
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure

docs.title: C++20 Principles Applied
docs.text:
• Concepts — template constraints (Updatable, Renderable, Damageable)
  • std::span — pass ranges without copies
  • RAII everywhere — no raw new/delete, only unique_ptr / shared_ptr
  • Composition > inheritance — Entity is a lightweight base; behaviors live in components
  • std::variant + std::visit — State Machine without pure virtuals
  • Logic / render separation — defender_lib has no display dependency

docs.title: Entity Hierarchy
docs.text:
classDiagram
    class Entity {
        <<abstract>>
        +update(dt: float) = 0
        +render(RenderTarget&) = 0
        +isAlive() bool
        #alive_ : bool
        #id_ : EntityId
    }

    class Tower {
        +update(dt: float)
        +render(RenderTarget&)
        +shoot(enemies: span~Enemy~)
        -range_ : float
        -fireRate_ : float
        -cooldown_ : float
        -stats_ : TowerStats
    }

    class Enemy {
        +update(dt: float)
        +render(RenderTarget&)
        +takeDamage(amount: float)
        +getPosition() Vector2f
        -type_ : EnemyType
        -element_ : Element
        -path_ : span~Vector2f~
        -pathIndex_ : size_t
        -health_ : float
        -speed_ : float
    }

    class Projectile {
        +update(dt: float)
        +render(RenderTarget&)
        -target_ : weak_ptr~Enemy~
        -damage_ : float
        -speed_ : float
    }

    Entity <|-- Tower
    Entity <|-- Enemy

docs.title: EntityManager
docs.text:
classDiagram
    class EntityManager {
        +addTower(pos: Vector2f, type: TowerType) Tower&
        +spawnEnemy(enemy: unique_ptr~Enemy~) Enemy&
        +nextId() EntityId
        +updateAll(dt: float)
        +renderAll(target: RenderTarget&)
        +removeDeadEntities()
        -towers_ : vector~unique_ptr~Tower~~
        -enemies_ : vector~shared_ptr~Enemy~~
        -projectiles_ : vector~unique_ptr~Projectile~~
    }

Enemies are shared_ptr so that Projectile can follow its target with a weak_ptr and notice when it died.

docs.title: EnemyFactory
docs.text:
Creates enemies at random, following probability matrices that depend on the map's biome. The species and the element are drawn independently:

P(type, element | biome) = P(type | biome) × P(element | biome)

classDiagram
    class EnemyFactory {
        +EnemyFactory(biome: Biome, seed: uint32, table: SpawnTable)
        +roll(rank: Rank) EnemySpec
        +create(id: EntityId, path: span~Vector2f~) unique_ptr~Enemy~
        +create(id: EntityId, spec: EnemySpec, path: span~Vector2f~, generation: int)$ unique_ptr~Enemy~
        +probability(element: Element) double
        +probability(type: EnemyType) double
        -weights_ : SpawnWeights
        -rng_ : mt19937
    }

    class EnemySpec {
        +type : EnemyType
        +element : Element
        +rank : Rank
    }

    class SpawnWeights {
        +elements : array~double, ELEMENT_COUNT~
        +types : array~double, ENEMY_TYPE_COUNT~
    }

    EnemyFactory --> SpawnWeights : one row per biome
    EnemyFactory ..> EnemySpec : rolls
    WaveManager --> EnemyFactory : builds waves

Default matrices (src/entities/EnemyFactory.cpp, in %):

Biome Water Fire Earth Wind Desert 10 35 35 20 Ice 45 5 15 35 Volcano 5 50 35 10 Forest 25 10 40 25 Biome Octopus Orangutan Cat Dog Duck Frog Desert 5 20 30 30 5 10 Ice 20 10 15 20 25 10 Volcano 10 25 25 20 10 10 Forest 10 30 15 15 15 15

Never 0%

Every weight must be > 0. A static_assert rejects the default table at compile time otherwise, and the constructor throws std::invalid_argument for a custom table. Adding an element (ice, magma, lightning...) leaves a 0 in every row until its column is filled, so it cannot be forgotten.

docs.title: Enemy definitions (stats + hooks)
docs.text:
An enemy is species + element + rank. All three are defined in C++, in src/entities/EnemyDefinitions.cpp, and each one brings stats and functions.

final stat = base(species) × mult(element) × mult(rank) + add(element) + add(rank)
Layer Struct Gives Species SpeciesDefinition base stats (baseStats(hp, speed, gold, damage)) + hooks Element ModifierDefinition multipliers (times) + bonuses (plus) + hooks Rank ModifierDefinition multipliers (times) + bonuses (plus) + hooks

Stats (Stats.hpp): Health, Speed, Reward, Damage, Scale.

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text:
EnemyHooks holds optional std::functions. The hooks of the three layers all run, species first, then element, then rank:

Hook Signature When onSpawn void(Enemy&) once, at creation onUpdate void(Enemy&, float dt) every frame while alive onHit float(Enemy&, float damage) before damage, returns the damage taken (chained) onDeath void(Enemy&, EnemySpawner&) killed by damage onReachBase void(Enemy&) reaches the base

A hook can change the enemy (enemy.stats()[Stat::Speed] *= 1.3f, enemy.heal(5)), and remember things in enemy.memory(0..3). Ready-made hooks: armor(n), regeneration(hpPerSecond), splitInto(count, rank).

{.description = "Dog: runs 30% faster once below half health.",
 .base = baseStats(80.f, 125.f, 8.f, 1.f),
 .hooks = {.onUpdate = [](Enemy& dog, float) {
     float& enraged = dog.memory(0);
     if (enraged == 0.f && dog.health() < dog.maxHealth() * 0.5f) {
         enraged = 1.f;
         dog.stats()[Stat::Speed] *= 1.3f;
     }
 }}},

docs.title: Current definitions
docs.text:
Layer Effect Orangutan slow tank, armor 2 Cat fast, survives its first deadly hit with 1 hp Dog +30% speed below half health Water +5 gold, regenerates 2 hp/s Fire ×1.15 speed, ×0.9 health Earth ×1.3 health, ×0.85 speed, armor 2 Wind ×1.3 speed, ×0.8 health Mini-boss ×4 health, ×3 gold/damage, ×0.9 speed, size ×1.4 Boss ×12 health, ×10 gold, ×5 damage, ×0.75 speed, armor 3, size ×1.9 Super boss ×25 health, ×20 gold, ×10 damage, ×0.6 speed, armor 5, size ×2.4, splits into 3 mini-bosses

Armor removes n from each hit but always lets 20% through; armor hooks stack.

docs.title: Super boss split
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant E as Enemy (super boss)
    participant B as EventBus
    participant W as WaveManager (EnemySpawner)
    participant M as EntityManager
    E->>B: EnemyKilled{enemy, reward}
    B->>W: handler
    W->>E: runDeathHooks(*this)
    E->>W: splitInto → rollSpec() ×3, spawnChild(parent, spec)
    Note over W: queued (we may be inside updateAll)
    W->>M: next update(): spawnEnemy(child), placed behind the parent

Children keep the element, roll their species with the biome matrices, and get generation + 1; splitting stops at MAX_SPAWN_GENERATION (3). A wave is not complete while children are waiting to spawn.

docs.title: Wave composition
docs.text: WAVE_RULES (EnemyDefinitions.hpp): 30 enemies in wave 1, +5 per wave, every 10th enemy is a mini-boss, the last one is a super boss, 0.7 s between spawns.

docs.title: EventBus (Decoupling)
docs.text:
classDiagram
    class EventBus {
        <<singleton>>
        +subscribe~T~(handler: function) HandlerId
        +unsubscribe(HandlerId)
        +emit~T~(event: T)
        -handlers_ : unordered_map
    }

    class EnemyReachedBase { +damage: float }
    class EnemyKilled { +reward: int }
    class TowerPlaced { +pos: Vector2f }
    class WaveStarted { +waveNumber: int }

    EventBus ..> EnemyReachedBase : emits
    EventBus ..> EnemyKilled : emits
    EventBus ..> TowerPlaced : emits
    EventBus ..> WaveStarted : emits

    class ResourceManager {
        <<RAII singleton>>
        +getTexture(id: TextureId) Texture&
        +getFont(id: FontId) Font&
        +getSoundBuffer(id: SoundId) SoundBuffer&
        -textures_ : unordered_map~TextureId, Texture~

docs.title: Game Loop
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant Main
    participant Game
    participant StateMachine
    participant PlayState
    participant EntityManager

    Main->>Game: run()
    loop 60 fps
        Game->>Game: pollEvents()
        Game->>StateMachine: handleEvent(event)
        Game->>StateMachine: update(dt)
        StateMachine->>PlayState: update(dt)
        PlayState->>EntityManager: updateAll(dt)
        PlayState->>EntityManager: removeDeadEntities()
        Game->>StateMachine: render(window)
        StateMachine->>PlayState: render(window)
        PlayState->>EntityManager: renderAll(window)
    end

docs.title: File Structure
docs.text:
Headers live in include/defender/<folder>/, sources in src/<folder>/.

src/
├── core/
│   ├── Game.hpp / Game.cpp
│   ├── StateMachine.hpp          ← std::variant<MenuState, PlayState, ...>
│   ├── EventBus.hpp              ← template header-only
│   ├── Events.hpp                ← EnemyKilled, WaveStarted...
│   └── Concepts.hpp              ← Updatable, Renderable, Damageable
├── states/
│   ├── MenuState.hpp / .cpp
│   ├── PlayState.hpp / .cpp
│   ├── PauseState.hpp / .cpp
│   └── GameOverState.hpp / .cpp
├── entities/
│   ├── Types.hpp                 ← Element, EnemyType, Rank, EnemySpec
│   ├── Stats.hpp                 ← Stat, EnemyStats
│   ├── EnemyDefinitions.hpp / .cpp ← species/element/rank stats + hooks, wave rules
│   ├── Entity.hpp                ← abstract base
│   ├── Tower.hpp / .cpp
│   ├── Enemy.hpp / .cpp
│   ├── EnemyFactory.hpp / .cpp   ← biome probability matrices
│   └── Projectile.hpp / .cpp
├── managers/
│   ├── EntityManager.hpp / .cpp
│   ├── WaveManager.hpp / .cpp

│   ├── MapGenerator.hpp / .cpp
│   └── MapRenderer.hpp / .cpp
└── defender_lib.cpp              ← CMake stub

docs.title: Workflows
docs.text: Workflow Trigger Action ci.yml Push / PR on main, develop Build + test release-drafter.yml PR merged to main Update release draft notes release.yml git push tag v*.*.* Build, package, publish release

docs.title: Release a New Version
docs.text:
git tag v0.2.0
git push origin v0.2.0

GitHub Actions will:

  1. Build the binary in Release mode
  2. Package it as defender-v0.2.0-linux-x86_64.tar.gz
  3. Publish it to the Releases page

docs.title: Conventional Commits → Auto-labels
docs.text:
PR titles follow Conventional Commits and are auto-labeled:

Prefix Label Release section feat: feature 🚀 New Features fix: bug 🐛 Bug Fixes perf: performance ⚡ Performance refactor: enhancement ✨ Enhancements docs: docs 📖 Documentation chore: / ci: / test: chore 🔧 Chores breaking: breaking 💥 Breaking Changes

Auto release notes

The release-drafter.yml workflow automatically maintains a draft release with categorized changelog entries based on merged PR titles. No manual changelog editing needed.

docs.title: Formatting — clang-format
docs.text:
Style: Allman, 4 spaces indentation, 100 columns max.

# Format all sources in-place
clang-format -i src/**/*.cpp include/**/*.hpp

docs.title: Linting — clang-tidy
docs.text:
Requires a compile_commands.json (generated by CMake).

# Generate compile commands first
cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=ON

# Run linter
clang-tidy -p build src/**/*.cpp

docs.title: Commit Convention
docs.text:
This project follows Conventional Commits:

<type>: <short description>

feat: add basic tower placement
fix: prevent enemies from clipping through walls
perf: cache path computation in WaveManager
refactor: extract EventBus to header-only template
docs: add architecture diagrams
chore: update CI to Ubuntu 22.04

Why Conventional Commits?

PR titles are parsed by the release-drafter workflow to auto-generate categorized release notes and apply labels automatically.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Tool Version CMake ≥ 3.21 GCC / Clang C++20 support (GCC ≥ 12, Clang ≥ 14) SFML deps Auto-fetched via FetchContent OpenAL libopenal-dev (for audio)

Install system dependencies (Ubuntu/Debian):

sudo apt-get install -y \
  cmake build-essential \
  libgl1-mesa-dev libudev-dev \
  libfreetype6-dev \
  libopenal-dev libvorbis-dev libflac-dev

docs.title: Build
docs.text:
# Configure
cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release

# Compile (parallel build)
cmake --build build --parallel

# Run
./build/src/defender

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
Tests are headless — no display required. They target defender_lib (game logic only, no SFML window).

# Configure in Debug mode
cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug

# Build
cmake --build build --parallel

# Run tests
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure

No display needed

The test suite runs on defender_lib which excludes SFML window code, making it suitable for CI environments without a display server.

docs.title: Release Builds
docs.text: The CI pipeline produces pre-built binaries for each tagged release. You can download them directly from the Releases page — no build required.
